# Cardinality of the Set of All Real-Valued Functions

## Setting Up the Problem

The set of all real-valued functions (on $\mathbb{R}$) is the set $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}}$, i.e., all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$.

The cardinality of this set is:
$$|\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}}| = |\mathbb{R}|^{|\mathbb{R}|} = \mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}}$$

## Computing $\mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}}$

Since $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$, I substitute:

$$\mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}} = \left(2^{\aleph_0}\right)^{2^{\aleph_0}}$$

Applying the cardinal exponent law $(a^b)^c = a^{b \cdot c}$:

$$\left(2^{\aleph_0}\right)^{2^{\aleph_0}} = 2^{\aleph_0 \cdot 2^{\aleph_0}}$$

## Simplifying the Exponent

I need to evaluate $\aleph_0 \cdot 2^{\aleph_0}$:

- By Cantor's theorem, $\aleph_0 < 2^{\aleph_0}$, so $\aleph_0 \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$.
- For infinite cardinals $\kappa$ and $\lambda \leq \kappa$: $\lambda \cdot \kappa = \kappa$.

Therefore:
$$\aleph_0 \cdot 2^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}$$

## Final Computation

Substituting back:
$$2^{\aleph_0 \cdot 2^{\aleph_0}} = 2^{2^{\aleph_0}} = 2^{\mathfrak{c}}$$

## Verification (Bounding)

- **Lower bound:** Since $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{R}} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}}$, we have $2^{\mathfrak{c}} \leq \mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}}$.
- **Upper bound:** Since $\mathfrak{c} \leq 2^{\mathfrak{c}}$, we have $\mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}} \leq (2^{\mathfrak{c}})^{\mathfrak{c}} = 2^{\mathfrak{c} \cdot \mathfrak{c}} = 2^{\mathfrak{c}}$.

By the Cantor–Bernstein–Schroeder theorem, $\mathfrak{c}^{\mathfrak{c}} = 2^{\mathfrak{c}}$.

## Conclusion

The cardinality of the set of all real-valued functions is indeed $2^{\mathfrak{c}}$.

$$\boxed{2^{\mathfrak{c}}}$$
